kin.form: 鵜草葺不合命 (Ugayafukiaezu-no-mikoto), 'Cormorant Thatching Unfinished'

pronunciation.note: Ugayafukiaezu is Tier 2: plain Hepburn. His strange name refers to a birth hut thatched with cormorant feathers and left unfinished. He is the immediate father of Emperor Jimmu.

domains.title: Cormorant Thatching Unfinished
domains.subtitle: Father of Jimmu and Link Between Sea and Land
domains.lead: Ugayafukiaezu is one of the most strangely named figures in Japanese myth. His name describes the unfinished thatched hut, covered with cormorant feathers, in which he was born. As the son of Hoori and the sea princess Toyotama, and the father of Emperor Jimmu, he is the final link between the ocean depths and the imperial line.

mythology.lead: Ugayafukiaezu's mythology is the final chapter of the Hoori-Toyotama story and the prelude to the reign of Jimmu.

myths.title: Birth in the Cormorant Hut
myths.text: After Toyotama returned to the sea, her son Ugayafukiaezu was born in a thatched hut. The name describes the hut's covering of cormorant feathers and its unfinished state. Toyotama's sister Tamayori came from the sea to raise him.

myths.title: Marriage to Tamayori
myths.text: Ugayafukiaezu grew up and married his aunt Tamayori, who had cared for him. Their union produced four sons, the youngest of whom was Kamuyamato-Iwarebiko, later known as Emperor Jimmu.

myths.title: Ancestor of the Imperial Line
myths.text: Through Ugayafukiaezu, the imperial line inherited both the maritime heritage of Toyotama and the terrestrial heritage of Hoori. His son Jimmu's eastern expedition founded the Yamato state.

lore.syncretism: Ugayafukiaezu is a genealogical figure whose strange name preserves the memory of archaic birth rituals and the alliance between sea and land. He has no independent cult but is essential to the imperial origin myth.
lore.culturalLegacy: Ugayafukiaezu is little known outside mythological and genealogical contexts, but his name is one of the most discussed in Japanese myth because of its obscurity. It preserves a fragment of ritual vocabulary that has otherwise been lost.
lore.extendedMeditation: Ugayafukiaezu is the child of an unfinished shelter. His name suggests that origins are messy, that birth happens in provisional spaces, and that the imperial line begins not in a palace but in a hut thatched with feathers and left open to the sky.
lore.archaeology: Ugayafukiaezu has no independent material cult. His significance is textual and genealogical, preserved in the Kojiki's account of the imperial lineage.
